articles.headline: Microsoft accelerates shift to homegrown AI chips to cut Nvidia dependence
articles.summary: Microsoft is moving more AI workloads onto its own chips, a sign that cloud providers are trying to control performance, power use and infrastructure costs. For businesses, this can affect future cloud pricing, service availability and the mix of AI services offered by major providers.

articles.headline: ASML warns chip equipment supply will fall short of demand in 2027 and 2028
articles.summary: ASML’s outlook suggests semiconductor capacity expansion could stay constrained longer than expected, which matters for companies relying on advanced chips, memory and AI infrastructure. Businesses planning large AI deployments may face tighter supply, longer lead times and continued cost pressure.

articles.headline: Policy changes on H-1B visas create new staffing risk for enterprise IT
articles.summary: Changes to H-1B policy could make it harder and more expensive for companies to hire specialized tech talent, especially in enterprise IT and engineering. That increases pressure on recruiting, retention and automation strategies for firms that depend on global technical labor.
